## Summary Accessibility/usability audit of `tools/bench-agent-cost/fixtures/design_target.html`, a synthetic "Account Settings" form fixture. Four violations are explicitly planted per the file's own header comment; I found two additional defects the comments don't call out. No edits made — audit only. ## User and task - **User segment**: any account holder, including keyboard-only and screen-reader users, updating account settings. - **Task**: enter/correct an email address and save. - **Success criterion**: the field's label, error state, and save action are perceivable and operable via keyboard and assistive technology, and the save completes. - **Failure modes**: label lost on input (placeholder-only), error not conveyed non-visually, save target unreachable by keyboard, close/dismiss control untouchable on mobile touch and unlabeled for AT. ## Stakes classification **High** — accessibility-critical form with error handling (skill's own High-stakes criteria: "accessibility-critical forms, error handling"). ## Findings ### 1. Email input has no persistent label (line 13) ```html ``` - **WCAG**: 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A) — and also 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A), since the input has no accessible name once the placeholder disappears on input/is unsupported by some AT. - **Severity**: High. Screen-reader users get no persistent field identity; sighted users lose the label the moment they type. - **Minimal fix**: add `` and `id="email"` on the input; the placeholder may stay as supplementary hint text, not the sole label. ### 2. Error state conveyed by color alone (line 17) ```html Invalid format ``` - **WCAG**: 1.4.1 Use of Color (A). Secondary: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / 3.3.1 Error Identification (A) — the error text is not programmatically associated with the input at all (no `aria-describedby`, no `id`), so even a screen-reader user who reaches the span gets no link between it and the field it describes. - **Severity**: High. Color-blind users get no signal; AT users get no association even if they perceive the text. - **Minimal fix**: prefix with a non-color indicator (e.g., an "Error:" text label or icon with accessible text) and wire it to the input via `aria-describedby="email-error"` plus `aria-invalid="true"` on the input when the error is shown. ### 3. Clickable `
` standing in for the Save button (lines 22–24) ```html
Save changes
``` - **WCAG**: 2.1.1 Keyboard (A) — not reachable or operable via keyboard. 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (AA) is moot since it never receives focus. 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A) — no `role="button"`, no accessible role at all (announced as generic text, not a control). - **Nielsen heuristic**: also fails "Consistency and standards" (a native interactive-looking element behaves as non-interactive to AT/keyboard). - **Severity**: Critical — this is the primary form-submission action and is entirely unusable without a mouse. - **Minimal fix**: replace the `
` with a native ``. (Per Move 4's enumerated refusals: a custom control replacing a native element is refused by default without full WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices conformance — trivially avoided here since a native ` ``` This line packs two distinct violations: **4a. Touch target size** - **WCAG**: 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (AA) — 16×16 CSS px is below the 24×24 px AA minimum (and well under the 44×44 px AAA target this repo's skill treats as canonical mobile guidance). - **Severity**: High on touch devices — the control is very likely to be mis-tapped or unreachable for users with motor impairments. - **Minimal fix**: set `min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px` (44×44 preferred) with padding to preserve the visual glyph size, or add adequate hit-area padding without visually enlarging the icon if that's a constraint. **4b. Empty `aria-label` overrides the visible glyph, leaving the button unnamed** - **WCAG**: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A) / 2.4.4 (analog) — `aria-label=""` is present and empty, which per the accessible-name computation takes precedence over the text content ("×"), so AT announces this as an unnamed button ("button" with no label) rather than falling back to the visible "×" text. - **Severity**: High. A screen-reader user has no way to know what this control does. - **Minimal fix**: either remove `aria-label=""` entirely (letting "×" be picked up, though "×" alone is a poor accessible name) or set a real value, e.g. `aria-label="Close"` / `aria-label="Dismiss"` matching the control's actual function. ## Heuristic evaluation | Heuristic | Pass/Fail | Evidence or fix | |---|---|---| | Visibility of system status | Fail | Error text (line 17) is not programmatically tied to the field it reports on — see Finding 2 | | Match between system and real world | Pass | N/A — no evidence of mismatch in this minimal fixture | | User control and freedom | Fail | Div-as-button (Finding 3) removes keyboard users' ability to invoke or escape the primary action | | Consistency and standards | Fail | Native controls (button, label) are avoided in favor of non-semantic markup (div, placeholder-as-label) | | Error prevention | N/A | Fixture has no validation-before-submit logic to evaluate | | Recognition rather than recall | Fail | Placeholder-only label (Finding 1) forces users to recall the field's purpose once they start typing | | Flexibility and efficiency of use | N/A | No evidence either way in this minimal fixture | | Aesthetic and minimalist design | Pass | Markup is minimal; no clutter | | Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors | Fail | "Invalid format" gives no guidance on the expected format and is not linked to the field (Finding 2) | | Help and documentation | N/A | Not applicable to a fixture this size | ## Component / token decisions N/A — this is a raw fixture with no design system to check against. ## Research evidence No "users want X" claims are made in this fixture or by me; all findings above are anchored to numbered WCAG 2.2 success criteria or a named Nielsen heuristic, per the skill's research-integrity check. ## Refusals applied - Custom clickable `
` replacing a native `
